extracted.intended_audience: regulated entities, environmental stakeholders, commenters, and legal practitioners interested in the Clean Air Act endangerment and cause-or-contribute findings
extracted.subtask_description: Preamble and response-to-comments guidance explaining how the Administrator should determine whether emissions from CAA section 202(a) source categories 'cause or contribute' to air pollution that endangers public health or welfare, and the statutory/procedural reviews applicable to such Findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Totality-of-the-circumstances test for contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: When exercising her judgment, the Administrator not only considers the cumulative impact, but also looks at the totality of the circumstances (e.g., the air pollutant, the air pollution, the nature of the endangerment, the type of source category, the number of sources in the source category, and the number and type of other source categories that may emit the air pollutant) when determining whether the emissions justify regulation under the CAA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is reasonable for an agency to adopt a totality-of-the-circumstances test; the Administrator should evaluate relative importance of source categories compared to other sources when viewed in context rather than applying a single mechanical test.

rubrics_metrics.name: No bright-line objective test of contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA may decline to establish a 'bright-line `objective' test of contribution.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is not a specific numerical bright line that must be achieved; numerical percentages are not treated and do not need to be treated as precise values. The Administrator may reasonably refrain from setting a single numeric cutoff for contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider unique global aspects of climate change in contribution analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Because climate change is a global problem resulting from global greenhouse gas emissions, the global nature of the problem justifies looking at contribution in a way that accounts for more numerous and varied sources and the absence of dominating sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Administrator may consider that lower percentage contributions (compared to local/regional problems) can nonetheless be meaningful in a global context; this approach is appropriate and not an attempt to regulate truly trivial or de minimis sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate relative importance of U.S. source categories in global context
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrator should evaluate how CAA section 202(a) source categories compare to other sources when viewed in the context of global emissions and U.S. national emissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the U.S. is a major emitter, comparing a U.S. source category's emissions to U.S. totals can be relevant to understanding its role in the global problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of existing emissions from current fleet as surrogate for future new-vehicle emissions
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA used the recent motor vehicle emissions inventory for the entire fleet as a surrogate for estimates of emissions for just new motor vehicles and engines, consistent with traditional practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: future projected emissions are uncertain; new vehicles are produced year in and year out and over time the fleet becomes composed of newer vehicles; emissions from new vehicles occur over their entire lifetime. Using recent fleet emissions introduces limited uncertainty but gives a reasonable, clear indication of relative magnitudes.

rubrics_metrics.name: No requirement to project future emissions from new source categories
rubrics_metrics.description: It was reasonable to use existing emissions from existing CAA section 202(a) source categories instead of projecting future emissions from new CAA section 202(a) source categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attempting to project future emissions would not provide greater accuracy or precision for the contribution comparison; current emissions data are a reasonable proxy for near-term emissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrator not limited to regulated subset when assessing contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: The contribution analysis need not be limited to only those CAA section 202(a) sources that the Administrator plans to regulate; the statutory text requires setting 'standards applicable to the emission of any air pollutant from [new motor vehicles], which in [her] judgment cause, or contribute to, air pollution which [endangers].' It does not tie the cause-or-contribute finding to the emissions reduced by a future standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions on cause/contribute and endangerment are separate from decisions on what emission standards to set; the Administrator need not (and cannot reasonably) anticipate the exact emission reductions that a future standard will achieve when making the contribution finding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid improperly integrating contribution finding with standards-setting
rubrics_metrics.description: The commenter's approach of limiting contribution to only the portion reduced by a future standard (or only reductions beyond other agencies' actions) finds no basis in statutory language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Administrator should not conflate the determination of whether emissions contribute to endangerment with subsequent determinations about what regulatory standards to adopt; the contribution finding should consider emissions absent action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare source emissions to both global and domestic emissions as appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: It is reasonable for the Administrator to look at how CAA section 202(a) source category emissions compare to global emissions on an absolute basis and also to consider how those source categories fit into the United States' emissions as a whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statute is silent on how to make the contribution analysis, so both global and domestic comparisons can be appropriate under the applicable science, facts, and law; using both perspectives is not arbitrary picking and choosing.

rubrics_metrics.name: No minimum 'more than minimal' numeric threshold required for contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Although commenters argued the law requires more than a minimal contribution, EPA declined to adopt a strict numerical standard and found that CAA section 202(a) emissions are anything but trivial under any interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Past EPA findings have accepted relatively small percentage contributions (e.g., 1.2% in Bluewater Network/Fairbanks) as sufficient; context and the nature of the pollution problem (global vs local) matter in assessing whether a contribution is meaningful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of precedent and comparative country-emission context
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA may consider that CAA section 202(a) source category total emissions are higher than most countries and are a significant part of the U.S. emissions inventory when evaluating contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparisons to other national emitters and to previous contribution findings support the reasonableness of the contribution determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Order 12866 (Regulatory Planning and Review) applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is a 'significant regulatory action' under EO 12866 because it raises novel policy issues, and EPA submitted this action to OMB for review under EO 12866.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an action raises novel policy issues or is otherwise significant, submit to OMB for review and document any OMB recommendations in the docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: This action does not impose an information collection burden under the PRA (44 U.S.C. 3501 et seq.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a rule or finding imposes information collection requirements, those must be evaluated under PRA; here the Findings do not create an information collection request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Flexibility Act (RFA) certification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: RFA generally requires an agency to prepare a regulatory flexibility analysis unless the agency certifies that the rule will not have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because these Findings do not impose any requirements, the Administrator certifies that the action will not have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities; where an action does impose requirements, EPA must assess impacts on small businesses, small governments, and small organizations per SBA definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfunded Mandates Reform Act (UMRA) applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: This action contains no Federal mandates under Title II of UMRA and imposes no enforceable duties on State, local, tribal governments or the private sector; therefore it is not subject to the UMRA requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an action contains federal mandates or regulatory requirements that might significantly or uniquely affect small governments, UMRA sections 202/205/203 apply; assess accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Order 13132 (Federalism) consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: This action does not have federalism implications because it does not impose requirements on any entities; EO 13132 does not apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an action will have substantial direct effects on States or the distribution of power, analyze federalism implications per EO 13132.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Order 13175 (Tribal consultation) consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: This action does not have tribal implications and does not impose enforceable duties on tribes; EO 13175 does not apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When actions may have direct effects on tribes or tribal governance, consult and coordinate as required by EO 13175.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Order 13045 (Protection of Children) applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: EO 13045 applies only to regulatory actions that concern health or safety risks such that the analysis could influence the regulation; these Findings do not establish an environmental standard intended to mitigate health or safety risks and thus are not subject to EO 13045.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider EO 13045 when a regulatory action will establish standards intended to mitigate health/safety risks and the analysis could influence regulatory decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Order 13211 (Significant energy actions) consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is not a 'significant energy action' under EO 13211 because it is not likely to have a significant adverse effect on the supply, distribution, or use of energy; it does not impose requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an action is likely to significantly affect energy supply/distribution/use, analyze impacts per EO 13211 and consider notice to DOE/OMB as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Technology Transfer and Advancement Act (NTTAA) consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: NTTAA directs EPA to use voluntary consensus standards in regulatory activities unless inconsistent with law or impractical; this action does not involve technical standards so EPA did not consider use of voluntary consensus standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For actions involving materials specifications, test methods, sampling procedures, or business practices, evaluate available voluntary consensus standards and document reasons for not using them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Order 12898 (Environmental Justice) consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: EO 12898 directs agencies to identify and address disproportionately high and adverse human health or environmental effects on minority and low-income populations; EPA determined these Findings will not have disproportionately high adverse effects because they do not affect the level of protection or impose requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where regulatory actions affect levels of protection or impose standards, analyze potential disproportionate impacts on minority and low-income populations and incorporate appropriate considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Congressional Review Act (CRA) reporting and major rule determination
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA will submit a report containing this rule and other required information to Congress and the Comptroller General under the CRA; this action is not a 'major rule' as defined in 5 U.S.C. 804(2) and will be effective January 14, 2010.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure CRA submission requirements are met and determine whether a rule qualifies as a 'major rule' affecting the effective date and congressional review process.
